card.statement:
Let $\cal A$ be an abelian category, $R$ be a continuously ordered $\mathbb R$-vector space,
$\cal B =$ mod-$B$ for some finite-dimensional algebra $B$, and $\gamma\in K_0(\cal A)$.
Suppose $\gamma$ is such that there exists an exact functor ${\cal F}:\cal B \to{\cal A}$ such that $\gamma={\cal F}(\beta)$ for some $\beta\in K_0(\cal \beta)$ and
$\cal F|_{\widetilde{\cal B}_\beta}: {\widetilde{\cal B}_\beta}\to {\widetilde{\cal A}_\gamma}$ is an equivalence of categories.
Then, for any slope function $\sigma:K_0(\widetilde{\cal A}_\gamma)\to R$, the moduli set ${\cal C}{\cal A}_\gamma^\sigma$ can be given a structure of projective $\mathbb{F}$-variety.
card.label: Theorem 7

paper.title: On Moduli Spaces for Abelian Categories
paper.abstract: We show that if A is an abelian category satisfying certain mild conditions, then one can introduce the concept of a moduli space of (semi)stable objects which has the structure of a projective algebraic variety. This idea is applied to several important abelian categories in representation theory, like highest weight categories.
